result.target_summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures address AMD's AI software strategy and ecosystem. D021 (2023) cites acquisitions to expand AI software capabilities within an open ecosystem. D012 (2024) details the strategy of providing a compelling user experience via the open ROCm software platform. This links the specific topic of the AI software ecosystem/platform.

previous_disclosures.summary: AMD views AI capabilities as central to its products, offering a roadmap for AI training and inference across cloud, edge, and endpoints, and expanded AI software capabilities in 2023 through the acquisitions of Mipsology SAS and Nod, Inc. to lower entry barriers for customers.

current_disclosures.summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure D012 outlines AMD's AI strategy (broad portfolio, ecosystem partnerships, open software). The 2025 disclosure D009 describes AMD's positioning as an end-to-end AI leader with a broad portfolio spanning cloud to endpoints. Both share the high-level strategic topic of AMD's AI leadership and portfolio breadth, though D006 also covers parts of this. D009 is the better semantic match for the 'Strategy' section content.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure outlined a specific 'AI strategy' with three distinct priorities (portfolio, partnerships, open software). The 2025 disclosure replaces this structured strategic framework with a broader, more aspirational positioning as an 'end-to-end AI leader' spanning cloud, edge, and endpoint. This shifts the disclosure from specific operational priorities to a high-level market positioning statement, representing a change in how the company articulates its strategic direction.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Shift from specific AI priorities to broad positioning

comparisons.peer_summary: The company's strategy focuses on technology leadership in semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, achieved through strategic acquisitions and internal R&D to maintain market leadership and drive diversified financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom articulate a strategy focused on technology leadership and delivering comprehensive hardware/software solutions. However, Broadcom explicitly emphasizes 'strategic acquisitions' and 'internal R&D' as the mechanisms to achieve this leadership and drive diversified results, whereas AMD frames its strategy around three specific priorities: adaptive hardware/software portfolio, ecosystem partnerships for scale, and the open ROCm software platform for deployment.

sentences.text: Our AI strategy is focused on three priorities.
The first is delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions.
The second is expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships we have established across the ecosystem to accelerate deployments of AMD based AI solutions at scale.

Our strategy is focused on technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions delivering a comprehensive suite of innovative infrastructure technology products to the world's leading business and government customers.

We seek to achieve this through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development, to ensure our products retain their technology market leadership.
This strategy results in a robust business model designed to drive diversified and sustainable operating and financial results.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's strategy to win is focused on four key themes: product competitiveness, open platforms, manufacturing at scale, and its people, leveraging its strengths in silicon, platforms, software, and packaging.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies define their core strategy around 'open platforms' and technological breadth. AMD explicitly lists 'expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships... to accelerate deployments' and using an 'open... software platform' as strategic priorities. Intel similarly lists 'open platforms' as one of its four key themes, committing to 'co-engineering' with software leaders to ensure 'software and hardware work better together,' reflecting a shared emphasis on ecosystem collaboration and openness, though Intel also heavily emphasizes 'manufacturing at scale' and 'product competitiveness' as distinct strategic pillars.

sentences.text: The second is expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships we have established across the ecosystem to accelerate deployments of AMD based AI solutions at scale.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.
We are uniquely positioned with the depth and breadth of our silicon, platforms, software, and packaging and process technology with at-scale manufacturing.

With these strengths and the tailwinds of the superpowers driving digital disruption, our strategy to win is focused on four key themes: product competitiveness, open platforms, manufacturing at scale, and our people.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron is an industry leader in innovative memory and storage solutions, delivering high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR products through Micron® and Crucial® brands to enable advances in AI and compute-intensive applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron frame their business strategy around delivering high-performance products to enable Artificial Intelligence and compute-intensive applications. AMD focuses on a 'broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions' and an 'open... software platform' to enable AI deployment. Micron similarly highlights its 'high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products' that 'fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications,' showing a parallel focus on hardware enabling AI workloads, albeit through memory/storage rather than processors.

sentences.text: The first is delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

With a relentless focus on our customers, technology leadership, and manufacturing and operational excellence, Micron delivers a rich portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products through our Micron® and Crucial® brands.

Every day, the innovations that our people create fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications that unleash opportunities - from the data center to the intelligent edge and across the client and mobile user experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA extends its leadership in AI by providing a complete end-to-end accelerated computing platform for training and inferencing, including GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs. The company supports this with DGX Cloud, NeMo for LLMs, a large developer ecosystem of over 4.7 million users, and educational initiatives like the Deep Learning Institute.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA describe a strategy centered on providing complete, end-to-end AI computing platforms that integrate hardware and software. AMD’s strategy is to deliver a 'broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions' and extend an 'open and proven software platform' to deploy AI broadly. NVIDIA similarly states it provides a 'complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI, addressing both training and inferencing,' supported by compute solutions (GPUs, CPUs, DPUs) and software like DGX Cloud and NeMo. Both emphasize the integration of hardware and software ecosystems to drive AI adoption.

And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.
We provide a complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI, addressing both training and inferencing.
Our compute solutions include all three major processing units in AI servers - GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs.

In addition, we offer DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform, and NeMo - a complete solution for building enterprise-ready Large Language Models, or LLMs, using open source and proprietary LLMs created by NVIDIA and third parties.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm emphasize the importance of a cohesive hardware and software architecture for AI. AMD’s strategy includes providing 'compelling user experiences' via an 'open and proven software platform' that enables its hardware to be deployed broadly. Qualcomm similarly details its 'System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture' with 'heterogeneous computing' features and the 'Qualcomm AI Engine' (including NPU and AI Stack) designed to enable 'high-performance and low-power computing' and allow developers to 'optimize and deploy AI models quickly.' Both highlight the integration of specialized hardware engines with software stacks to enable AI capabilities.

sentences.text: The first is delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.

The Qualcomm® AI Stack is a unified AI software portfolio designed to help developers optimize and deploy AI models quickly using our chipset solutions by supporting AI frameworks and runtimes, developer libraries, system software and popular operating systems.
